entries.name: 911 (emergency)
entries.summary: For any emergency that needs police, fire or an ambulance right now. Stay on the line until the call-taker says you can hang up. Texting 911 works only in some places; a voice call is the most reliable.

contact.note: Only where your local 911 centre accepts texts; if not, you get a bounce-back message. Call if you can.

entries.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
entries.summary: Trained counsellors for anyone in emotional distress, thoughts of suicide, a mental-health or substance-use crisis, or worried about someone else. Text and chat are also offered in Spanish.

entries.name: Veterans Crisis Line
entries.summary: Crisis support for Veterans, service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and the people who support them. You do not need to be enrolled in VA benefits or health care.

entries.name: Crisis Text Line
entries.summary: Text with a live, trained volunteer crisis counsellor about anything that feels too heavy: anxiety, grief, self-harm, suicide, relationships and more.

entries.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
entries.summary: Advocates for anyone experiencing abuse in a relationship, or worried about someone who is. The site also has an automated chat; ask for a live advocate if you want a person.

entries.name: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
entries.summary: A safe, non-judgemental place for anyone concerned about or affected by child abuse. It is not a reporting line and is not connected to 911; to make a report, use your state's child-abuse reporting number.

entries.name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
entries.summary: Confidential help and tips for anyone who is, or knows someone who is, being forced or coerced into work or sex. Its website is also in Spanish.

contact.note: Live chat is not always open; the phone line is 24/7

entries.name: RAINN National Sexual Assault Hotline
entries.summary: Support for survivors of sexual violence and the people who love them, by phone, chat or text, in English and Spanish.

entries.name: SAMHSA National Helpline
entries.summary: A U.S. government information and referral line for people and families facing mental-health or substance-use problems: local treatment, support groups and community services, in English and Spanish.

entries.name: 211 (United Way)
entries.summary: One number for local help of every kind: food, housing, bills, health and crisis services. Calls are confidential. In a few places the local 211 is not open around the clock; see the city pages.

entries.name: Option Line
entries.summary: Pregnancy help by phone, text and live chat for anyone facing an unplanned pregnancy, with a finder for a pregnancy help centre near you. Listed by Heartbeat International as part of its work.

entries.name: Heartbeat International — Worldwide Directory of Pregnancy Help
entries.summary: A searchable directory of pregnancy help centres, run by Heartbeat International.

entries.name: Care Net — Pregnancy Decision Line
entries.summary: Care Net's helpline for anyone facing an unexpected pregnancy decision, whether considering abortion, adoption or parenting. It also links to Care Net pregnancy centres, which it says number more than 1,350 across North America.
entries.hours: Mon–Thu 9am–5pm, Fri 9am–4pm (Eastern)

entries.name: Abortion Pill Rescue Network (Abortion Pill Reversal)
entries.summary: For a woman who has started a medication (pill) abortion and regrets it: the helpline connects her with a medical professional nearby. The site says the outcome of any reversal attempt cannot be guaranteed.
entries.hours: 24/7 helpline

entries.name: Standing With You
entries.summary: Help for pregnant and parenting women, including students and workers: talk with a person by phone or text and search a directory of local pregnancy resources. It says it is a directory and is not affiliated with every resource it lists.

entries.name: Support After Abortion
entries.summary: Compassionate, non-judgemental support for women and men affected by abortion, and a network of healing providers.
entries.hours: Mon–Fri 9am–5pm (Eastern)

entries.name: Rachel's Vineyard
entries.summary: Weekend retreats for women and men hurting after abortion, held in more than 375 locations. Retreats are Catholic, and its listings say all faiths are welcome.

entries.name: Surrendering the Secret
entries.summary: An eight-part Bible study for healing after abortion, for women and men. It can connect you with one of more than 6,000 certified leaders by phone, email, online or in person.

contact.note: Ask to be connected with a leader

entries.name: Project Rachel (HopeAfterAbortion.org)
entries.summary: A Church ministry of healing after abortion. Choose your state to find someone near you; some local ministries also answer a national toll-free line.

contact.note: 888-456-HOPE; connects to a participating local ministry

entries.name: Safe Haven Baby Boxes
entries.summary: For a parent in crisis who cannot care for a newborn: a 24-hour hotline, and boxes in fire stations and hospitals where a newborn can be surrendered safely and anonymously under the Safe Haven law.
entries.hours: 24-hour hotline

entries.name: National Safe Haven Alliance
entries.summary: A crisis helpline for parents considering giving up an infant under their state's Safe Haven law, with help to parent, to plan an adoption, or to find a safe haven location. In an emergency, call 911.

entries.name: One More Child
entries.summary: Christ-centred services for single moms, hungry children, trafficked children, foster children and struggling families. Headquarters in Lakeland, Florida.

entries.name: Lifeline Children's Services
entries.summary: Christian adoption, foster care and family support, and free, confidential, no-pressure counselling for a mother deciding whether adoption is right for her.

contact.note: For a pregnant mother considering adoption

entries.name: Feeding America — find your local food bank
entries.summary: Enter your ZIP code to find the food bank that serves your area; the food bank can point you to pantries and meal sites near you.

entries.name: USDA National Hunger Hotline
entries.summary: Staff find food near you: meal sites, food banks, government programmes and other services. Operated by Hunger Free America for the USDA.

contact.note: Automated; text a word such as "food" with your address or ZIP code

entries.hours: Mon–Fri 8am–8pm (Eastern)

entries.name: The Salvation Army — location finder
entries.summary: Find the nearest Salvation Army centre and the services it offers, such as food, shelter and emergency help.

entries.name: GriefShare
entries.summary: Weekly support groups, in person and online, for people grieving the death of a family member or friend. Each meeting has a video, discussion and a participant guide; groups are hosted by churches, and the guide costs from nothing to about $25. If grief turns into a crisis, call or text 988.

entries.name: Celebrate Recovery
entries.summary: A biblically based recovery ministry, hosted by churches, for anyone seeking healing from hurts, hang-ups and habits, with a weekly online meeting (Wednesdays 12pm Pacific). Its help page says: if you are in danger of hurting yourself or someone else, call 911, or call or text 988.

entries.name: FindTreatment.gov (SAMHSA)
entries.summary: The U.S. government's locator for treatment of substance use and mental-health conditions. For a person on the phone, call the SAMHSA National Helpline (1-800-662-4357).

entries.hours: Office 8am–4pm

entries.name: Downtown Ecumenical Services Council (DESC)

entries.hours: Groceries and clothing Mon, Wed, Fri 9am–12pm

entries.name: Catholic Charities Jacksonville — drive-thru food pantry
entries.summary: Serves people of all faiths. Tickets from 8am for up to 60 households; one ticket per household; food from 10:30am.
entries.hours: Wednesdays and Fridays (arrive about 8am)

entries.name: Lutheran Social Services of Northeast Florida
entries.summary: Food pantry by appointment, plus refugee services, HIV care and financial coaching.

entries.name: Jewish Family & Community Services (LJD JFCS)
entries.summary: Counselling, the Max Block Food Pantry, financial assistance and family services, available to all in Northeast Florida. The map point is the food pantry; the main office is at 8540 Baycenter Rd (Mon–Fri 8:30am–5pm).

entries.hours: Food pantry Tue & Thu 10am–12pm

entries.name: City Rescue Mission — Shelter Care
entries.summary: Emergency meals and shelter, and the way into its LifeBuilders addiction-recovery programme. Anyone in need may come for dinner.
entries.hours: Dinner for guests not staying overnight 4:30–5:30pm

entries.name: Trinity Rescue Mission
entries.summary: Emergency services downtown: meals, shelter, showers, clothing and hygiene kits, and help into programmes to end homelessness.

entries.name: Sulzbacher — Downtown Campus (men)
entries.summary: Short-term housing for men, daily meals, health care (Duval Family Health) and an Urban Rest Stop; community lunch and dinner are open to anyone. Walk-in requirements: state ID and a free shelter clearance card from the Duval County Health Department (515 W. 6th St, 904-630-3300).

entries.name: Sulzbacher Village (women and families)
entries.summary: Short-term housing for women and families. Bring birth certificates and Social Security cards for all family members.
entries.hours: Walk-in Mon–Thu 8–11am

entries.name: The Salvation Army — Jacksonville Social Services / Red Shield Lodge
entries.summary: Social services and the Red Shield Lodge at the same address. Call for current hours and help available.

entries.name: Community Hospice & Palliative Care — Grief and Bereavement
entries.summary: Individual, family and children's grief counselling, support groups, and workshops. Free to hospice families for 13 months; selected services free to the whole community.

entries.name: Beaches Emergency Assistance Ministry (BEAM)
entries.summary: Runs a food pantry by appointment for residents of the beaches-area ZIP codes it lists (32233, 32266, 32250, 32082, 32224, 32227, 32228) and for active-duty military. Bring a photo ID and proof of address, and call to request an appointment up to seven days ahead.

contact.note: call to request a pantry appointment

entries.address: 850 6th Avenue S., Ste 400, Jacksonville Beach, FL 32250

entries.name: Bridge The Gap, Inc.
entries.summary: Gives out food to the public on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, and also delivers to seniors and people with disabilities. Call 904-799-5406 to confirm the current schedule.
entries.hours: Tuesday and Thursday 10:00 am-12:00 pm (public/community distribution)

entries.name: Community Health Outreach (Westjax Outreach Inc.) - The Lord's Pantry
entries.summary: An outreach whose stated mission is to glorify God and show the love of Jesus Christ; its food pantry, the Lord's Pantry, hands out groceries on Saturday mornings by drive-thru or walk-up. It also runs medical and dental clinics for low- to no-income uninsured residents.
entries.hours: Saturdays 7:30-8:30 am (drive-thru and walk-up)

entries.name: Cornerstone Chosen Ministries - Food Pantry
entries.summary: A church that runs a food pantry on Sundays at noon; its Sunday worship service is at 10 am. Call to confirm before going, because the page gives no eligibility details.
entries.hours: Food pantry Sundays at 12 noon (Sunday service 10 am)

entries.name: Barnabas Center
entries.summary: A Nassau County community-services centre whose food pantry gives free groceries (currently drive-through) to food-insecure Nassau County adults, twice a month. Bring a photo ID and proof of Nassau County residency; its separate mobile food distributions are open to everyone.
entries.hours: Pantry Tuesday-Friday 10 am-12 pm
entries.address: 1303 Jasmine Street, Suite 101, Fernandina Beach, FL 32034

entries.name: The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center - Jacksonville
entries.summary: A faith-based, long-term residential work-therapy programme for adults struggling with alcohol and substance abuse. Call 904-641-2122 to ask about admission.
entries.cost: Generally at no cost to participants, per its page

entries.name: Celebrate Recovery - Trinity Baptist Church (Hammond location)
entries.summary: A weekly Celebrate Recovery group that meets Sunday evenings in the south end of the D building at Trinity Baptist's Hammond location, with childcare for birth through fifth grade.

contact.note: Celebrate Recovery contact named on the page
church main number, from its contact page

entries.hours: Sundays: large group 5:55 pm, small groups 6:55 pm

contact.note: Information and Assessment Center / Gateway Connect

entries.name: Community Health Outreach - Baby Luv
entries.summary: A weekly distribution of infant supplies, paired with client-choice grocery shopping in its pantry; the organisation says it serves people who lack baby supplies such as diapers and formula. The page does not say who qualifies, so call first.
entries.hours: Wednesdays 9:00-11:00 am

entries.name: First Coast Women's Services - Clay County Center

entries.name: Women's Help Center - Callahan

entries.hours: Monday-Thursday 9 am-2 pm

entries.name: Youth Crisis Center

contact.note: toll-free, for callers outside Duval County

entries.name: Mental Health Resource Center (MHRC) Emergency Services - MHRC North
entries.summary: Emergency mental health services that screen adults, adolescents and children for inpatient admission and give telephone or face-to-face assessments and referrals to people who are not admitted. The page does not say whether walk-ins are accepted, so call first.

entries.name: The Market at St. Mary's (St. Mary's Episcopal Church Outreach)
entries.summary: A church food pantry for individuals and families without enough food. Its page gives no hours, so call before going.

entries.name: Bethany Ministries - Bethany Christian Cupboard

entries.hours: Tuesday and Thursday 5:30-6:30 pm

entries.address: 2251 St. Johns Bluff Rd S, Jacksonville, FL 32246

entries.name: Redeemer Episcopal Church - Food Pantry
entries.summary: A church food pantry open on Wednesday mornings. The page does not say who is eligible.
entries.hours: Wednesdays 8:30-11:30 am

entries.name: My Brother's Keeper Food Pantry (St. Clement Catholic Church)

entries.hours: Fridays 8:00 a.m.-12:00 noon; closed the first Friday of every month.
entries.address: 1104 N Alexander St, Plant City, FL 33563

entries.name: ACTS Florida - Outpatient Program (Agency for Community Treatment Services)
entries.summary: Outpatient counselling and treatment for substance use and behavioural health in north Tampa. Assessments take place at this office on a walk-in basis. The first assessment costs $65, and after that payment follows a sliding fee scale.
entries.hours: Assessment hours: Monday-Thursday 9 a.m.-4 p.m.; Friday 9 a.m.-2 p.m.

entries.name: ACTS Florida - Addictions Receiving Facility (adult and juvenile)
entries.summary: A 24-hour facility for people in crisis from alcohol or drug use, with detox and immediate care for adults and crisis help for juveniles and their families. entries.hours: Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
entries.address: 3107 N 50th St, Suite A, Tampa, FL 33619

entries.name: Ibis Healthcare - Men's Residential Substance Use Treatment
entries.summary: A residential recovery program that houses adult men during treatment. The admissions line is answered around the clock for admission questions and crisis support, and a clinical assessment is done when you arrive. Ibis says it accepts several insurances (including Medicaid, Medicare and the Hillsborough County Health Plan), offers sliding fees, and denies no one for inability to pay.

contact.note: Number listed on the Ibis contact page

entries.hours: Program hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; admissions phone line 24/7

entries.name: Recovery Church Tampa
entries.summary: A church for people in recovery, meeting on Saturday evenings at The Resting Place Church. It calls itself a local independent church in partnership with the Association of Recovery Churches, under the heading 'Finding Freedom in Christ'.
entries.hours: Saturdays at 7:00 PM

entries.name: Celebrate Recovery at First Baptist Church of Riverview
entries.summary: A 12-step recovery program for anyone struggling with hurt, pain or addiction of any kind. Each week has worship, time working the 12 steps and 8 recovery principles, and sharing. Childcare is available on request only.
entries.hours: Every Monday night at 6:45 PM

entries.name: Ibis Healthcare - Adult Mental Health Crisis Care (walk-in crisis center)
entries.summary: A walk-in crisis center for adults in a mental-health crisis, open every day and night with no appointment needed for an immediate evaluation. entries.hours: Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year

entries.name: Ibis Healthcare - Children's Crisis Services (walk-in)
entries.summary: Walk-in crisis evaluations for children and teens ages 5-17 in a mental-health emergency; no appointment is needed. Ibis says no one is denied treatment for lack of insurance or ability to pay. For immediate safety concerns, call 911.
entries.hours: Available 24/7, 365 days a year

entries.name: Ibis Healthcare - Community Housing Solutions Center
entries.summary: Emergency bridge housing for adult men and women experiencing homelessness in Hillsborough County, for up to 120 days and up to 75 people at a time. Call or walk in for a short screening; you do not need ID or paperwork to start.
entries.hours: Walk-in screenings Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-12:00 PM; administration Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM

entries.name: Children's Board Family Resource Center - Brandon
entries.summary: A Children's Board of Hillsborough County family centre with a free-play space for children and caregivers, parent classes and support groups, early childhood service coordination (help making a support plan and getting referrals), and a computer lab with printing, scanning and faxing. The notary service is stated to be at no cost.
entries.hours: Mondays and Saturdays 9:00am-5:00pm; Tuesdays and Thursdays 9:00am-7:00pm; Wednesdays and Fridays 9:00am-6:00pm

entries.name: Children's Board Family Resource Center - Plant City
entries.summary: A Children's Board of Hillsborough County family centre with a free-play space for children and caregivers, parent classes and support groups, early childhood service coordination (help making a support plan and getting referrals), and a computer lab with printing, scanning and faxing. The notary service is stated to be at no cost. This is the only center with the MOSI in Motion STEAM exhibit, open to families at no cost.
entries.hours: Mondays and Saturdays 9:00am-5:00pm; Tuesdays and Thursdays 9:00am-7:00pm; Wednesdays and Fridays 9:00am-6:00pm
entries.address: 301 N Palmer St, Plant City, FL 33563

entries.name: Bay Chapel Food Pantry
entries.summary: A Christian ministry pantry in New Tampa that gives out groceries to anyone in need in Hillsborough County, in partnership with Feeding Tampa Bay (USDA TEFAP).

entries.address: 19911 Bruce B Downs Blvd, Tampa, FL 33647

entries.name: Hope Effect Food Pantry
entries.summary: A Christian nonprofit's food pantry on W Linebaugh Ave serving families across Hillsborough County with groceries, produce, meat and other essentials. Each household may visit once a week; closed on major holidays and sometimes in extreme weather.
entries.hours: Every Thursday 2-3 PM and every Sunday 9-10 AM

entries.name: Calvary Community Cupboard (Calvary Lutheran Church)
entries.summary: Volunteer-run food pantry established in 1979, open to residents of Ruskin, Apollo Beach, Riverview, Sun City and Wimauma. The pantry is at capacity: new registrations are taken only on the first Monday of each month. The page also lists the church campus as 1250 E College Ave, so confirm the entrance by phone.
entries.hours: Tuesdays 7:30-10:00 AM

entries.name: Redeemer Church Riverview - Food Pantry
entries.summary: Church food pantry open twice a month. The page says the pantry's passion is to serve the poor, helpless and homeless; it lists no eligibility rules.
entries.hours: 1st Thursday of each month 9-11 AM and 3rd Thursday of each month 5-7 PM

entries.name: Matthew 25 Outreach Ministry (St. Lawrence Catholic Church)
entries.summary: Parish ministry giving out food by drive-through twice a month at the Sandra Tini Outreach Center; also does weekly Cereal Saturdays.
entries.hours: 2nd and 4th Sundays of each month, 1:30 PM-3:30 PM

entries.name: Berkeley Food Pantry (Berkeley Preparatory School)
entries.summary: Client-choice pantry run by Berkeley Preparatory School as part of Feeding Tampa Bay's Feeding Minds school pantry program, serving the Town 'N' Country neighbourhood with food, clothes and other necessities. The phone is the school's contact for the pantry.
entries.hours: Open every other Saturday, 9-11 a.m.

entries.name: Metropolitan Ministries - Metro Market (East Tampa, Prosperity Center)
entries.summary: Grocery market of fresh produce, bread, meat and pantry staples, at the Prosperity Center at Thaddeus M. Bullard Academy. You can visit once a month and must be able to store and cook food at home; a utility bill, lease or rental receipt and an assessment are required.

entries.name: Nativity Catholic Church - Food Pantry (Brandon/Valrico)
entries.summary: Parish food pantry for families in the Brandon/Valrico area; registration is required before receiving food and the page says the next registration window is to be announced, so call before going.
entries.hours: Thursdays 11:00 AM-12:00 PM

entries.name: Celebrate Recovery Tampa (South Tampa Fellowship, Ballast Point campus)

The phone is the church's main number from its own site; the recovery page itself lists no phone.
entries.hours: Thursdays at 6:30 p.m.

entries.name: Children's Board Family Resource Center - South County

entries.hours: Mondays and Saturdays 9:00am-5:00pm; Tuesdays and Thursdays 9:00am-7:00pm; Wednesdays and Fridays 9:00am-6:00pm

lines.summary: A Monroe-based service for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault and child abuse. The page lists separate crisis lines for domestic violence and for sexual assault, and says its shelter location is not shared publicly for clients' safety.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: SECU Youth Crisis Center (Monarch)
lines.summary: A crisis programme for young people aged 6 to 17 in a mental health or substance use crisis, taking referrals from all North Carolina counties. The page says walk-ins are not accepted, so call ahead to check it is the right service.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

entries.name: Nashville Rescue Mission - Linda & Mike Curb Men's Center
entries.summary: A Christ-centered mission serving people who are hungry, hurting or homeless, with emergency services and a Life Recovery Program. This is the men's center (men 18 and older).

entries.name: Nashville Rescue Mission - Linda & Mike Curb Women's Center
entries.summary: The women's center of the Christ-centered Nashville Rescue Mission, which serves people who are hungry, hurting or homeless. Call the general line for meal and shelter details.

entries.name: Room In The Inn
entries.summary: Nashville nonprofit offering support services, a winter shelter, recuperative care and transitional and permanent housing for people experiencing homelessness. The page gives no hours; call first.

entries.name: Safe Haven Family Shelter
entries.summary: Shelter and housing programs for homeless families with children. Referrals come through Nashville's Coordinated Entry (615-862-6444) rather than walk-ins, so call first.

contact.note: Coordinated Entry, to start a referral

entries.name: The Salvation Army Nashville - Center of Hope
entries.summary: Gives out sack lunches for lunch and dinner. Rent and utility help must be requested online at sahelp.org, not by phone. The Salvation Army states its mission is to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ and meet human needs in His name.

contact.note: 1-800-SAL-ARMY, the number on the Nashville site

entries.hours: Sack lunches Monday to Friday, 11:00 am-12:30 pm and 3:00-4:30 pm, or until they run out

entries.name: Nashville Family Safety Center
entries.summary: Metro Nashville center where people harmed by domestic violence can get help in one place, including order-of-protection help. Hours differ between Metro pages, so phone before you go.
entries.hours: Monday-Friday, 9 a.m.-6 p.m. (per the Safety Centers page)

entries.name: Sexual Assault Center
entries.summary: Support for survivors of sexual assault, with a 24-hour crisis line and a SAFE Clinic that is open 24/7 (615-258-5888).
entries.hours: Office: Monday-Thursday 8 am-4 pm, Friday 8 am-2 pm

entries.name: Nashville Children's Alliance
entries.summary: Child advocacy center for children and families affected by child abuse, offering forensic interviews, family advocacy and therapy. The page lists no hours; call first.

entries.name: Alive Hospice - Grief Support
entries.summary: Grief support for children, teens and adults after the death of someone significant, open to anyone in the community whether or not their loved one was in Alive's care. Hours are not listed.
entries.cost: Youth and family programs free except camp and retreat; counseling sliding scale; scholarships available

entries.name: Hope Clinic for Women
entries.summary: Faith-based clinic offering free pregnancy tests, ultrasounds and options consultations, plus counseling that includes pregnancy loss and post-abortion support. It says it does not perform or refer for abortions.
entries.hours: Monday-Thursday 9am-4:30pm; Friday 9am-2pm; closed weekends

entries.name: Pregnancy Care Center of Tennessee - Old Hickory
entries.summary: Pregnancy center in the Old Hickory area offering free, confidential help to people facing an unplanned pregnancy.
entries.hours: Monday-Wednesday 9am-5pm; Thursday 12pm-7pm
entries.cost: Free (the page says all services are free and confidential)

entries.name: AGAPE
entries.summary: Christian social-service agency offering counseling, foster care, adoption, maternity support for unplanned pregnancies and domestic-violence care. The page lists no office hours.

entries.name: Samaritan Center (Temple Church)
entries.summary: North Nashville church ministry serving daily hot lunches, free clothing and referrals. The page gives no meal times; call first.

entries.name: The Branch of Nashville - Food Pantry
entries.summary: Food pantry serving the Southeast Nashville area by online appointment, with one emergency box per family per month without an appointment. Bring a valid ID.
entries.hours: Mon-Tue 9:30am-2pm; Wed 10am-2pm; Fri closed; Sat 9:30am-12:30pm (by appointment or emergency walk-in)

entries.name: Donelson First Food Pantry
entries.summary: Church food pantry for people in need in the Donelson area. Call the church office to ask what to bring.
entries.hours: Wednesday 5-6 p.m.; Thursday 10-11 a.m.

entries.name: Christian Cooperative Ministry
entries.summary: Food pantry in Madison. The page does not state who qualifies; call to ask.
entries.hours: Monday-Thursday 9:00 am-2:00 pm; last order 1:30 pm

entries.name: Catholic Charities, Diocese of Nashville
entries.summary: Main office of the diocese's charity. Its site says pantries operate at its Family Resource Centers; call to learn which site serves your area.
entries.hours: Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m., except holidays

entries.name: Celebrate Recovery at Christ Church Nashville
entries.summary: Weekly church-based recovery meeting, with a dinner first.
entries.hours: Fridays: dinner 5:45-6:30 pm, service 6:30-8:30 pm
entries.geocode: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Census geocoder found no match)

entries.name: Celebrate Recovery at West End Community Church
entries.summary: Weekly Christ-centered recovery community with dinner, large group and small groups. No phone listed; email the care pastor.
entries.hours: Thursdays: dinner 5:45 pm, large group 6:30-7:30, small groups 7:40-8:30
entries.cost: Dinner $5 per person, $10 family maximum; free childcare

entries.name: Martha O'Bryan Center
entries.summary: East Nashville center helping families with children and caregivers through coaching, parenting programs, early learning and education. Hours are not listed.

entries.name: Bethlehem Centers of Nashville
entries.summary: Community family resource center with programs for families, children, youth and seniors 55 and older. Hours are not listed.

entries.name: St. Luke's Community House - The Pantry at St. Luke's
entries.summary: A food pantry for any Davidson County resident, in the Charlotte Park/West Nashville area. No appointment is needed; you can shop once per calendar month. First-time visitors bring photo ID, proof of Davidson County residence, and ID for everyone in the household.
entries.hours: Pantry: Tuesday-Friday 10 AM-2:30 PM, plus Tuesday 4-6 PM. Office: Monday-Friday 8:30 AM-4:30 PM.

entries.name: Madison Church of Christ Benevolence Center
entries.summary: A church food pantry (run with Second Harvest Food Bank) for residents of the 37115 ZIP code, plus a clothing room where volunteers help people choose what they need. Open every weekday morning.
entries.hours: Weekdays 8:30 a.m.-11:30 a.m.

entries.name: Catholic Charities Loaves & Fishes (Holy Name Parish Center)
entries.summary: Hot community meals served in the Parish Center of Holy Name Catholic Church in East Nashville. Open to anyone in need, with no restrictions based on religion, race, or proof of need.
entries.hours: Every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday: breakfast 8:30-9:30 a.m., lunch 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m.

entries.name: Nourish Food Bank - Nashville/Glencliff
entries.summary: A food pantry that gives out food, hygiene and cleaning supplies, and infant products. Everyone is welcome (some programs have income rules). You fill out a form, wait for your number to be called, and do a short intake before receiving food.
entries.hours: Tuesday 5:30-7:30 p.m.; Saturday 12:00-3:00 p.m.

entries.name: Catholic Charities Family Resource Center at C. E. McGruder
entries.summary: A North Nashville center offering an emergency food pantry, help with rent and utility referrals, counseling and life-skills programs, and job training. It serves people in a listed set of ZIP codes (37072, 37080, 37115, 37143, 37189, 37205, 37207, 37208, 37209, 37216, 37218, 37221, 37228).
entries.hours: Food pantry: Monday-Thursday, 9:00 a.m.-3:30 p.m.

entries.name: Catholic Charities Family Resource Center at Casa Azafran
entries.summary: A South Nashville center with an emergency food pantry, short-term case management, emergency housing assistance, financial literacy and job-seeking help, and Hispanic family services. It serves people in a listed set of ZIP codes (37013, 37076, 37138, 37203, 37204, 37206, 37210, 37211, 37212, 37215, 37217, 37220).
entries.hours: Food pantry: Monday-Thursday, 9:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m. Center: weekdays 9:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m.
entries.geocode: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Census geocoder found no match)

entries.name: Community Care Fellowship
entries.summary: A Christian ministry in East Nashville for people experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity. Daily breakfast and three lunches a week (each with a short devotion), plus showers, laundry, hygiene items, clothing, phone, Wi-Fi and mail service.
entries.hours: Open Monday-Friday 9 a.m.-3 p.m. Breakfast Mon-Fri 9-9:30 a.m.; lunch Tue, Thu, Fri 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m.; to-go lunch Sundays 12:30 p.m.; showers Mon-Fri 9 a.m.-1 p.m.; clothing Mon-Fri 1-3 p.m.

entries.name: Mental Health Cooperative - Crisis Treatment Center
entries.summary: A walk-in psychiatric crisis center for adults, open around the clock with no appointment needed. A separate 24/7 crisis stabilization unit for children and youth ages 4-17 is next door at 260A Cumberland Bend. Mobile crisis teams can also come to you.
entries.hours: Open 24/7, 365 days a year

entries.name: Mental Health Cooperative - Nashville (substance use and mental health care)
entries.summary: A nonprofit clinic offering outpatient addiction treatment, medication-assisted treatment, peer recovery support and mental health care. Walk-ins are welcome on weekdays or you can make an appointment. It serves people with TennCare and those who qualify for state-funded programs; a sliding fee scale is available and it says no one is denied care for inability to pay.

contact.note: substance use services; page lists it as 24/7

entries.hours: Office hours Monday-Friday 8 AM-4:30 PM; walk-ins welcome or by appointment

entries.name: Cumberland Heights - River Road campus
entries.summary: A long-established nonprofit addiction treatment center on a 177-acre campus beside the Cumberland River, with 24/7 detox, residential treatment for adults and young men, and outpatient care. Call admissions first for a confidential assessment; it takes insurance and self-pay.

entries.name: The Next Door Recovery - Nashville
entries.summary: A faith-based addiction treatment program for women: medically monitored detox, a 28-day residential program, and outpatient care. It gives priority to pregnant women and mothers and says care is accessible to women who are uninsured or underinsured. Admissions line is staffed around the clock.
entries.hours: Admissions 24/7

entries.name: Centerstone Nashville - Dede Wallace Campus
entries.summary: A nonprofit behavioral health center listing counseling, addiction recovery, outpatient care, psychiatric care, crisis services, and children and family services at this campus. Call the initial-appointments line first.

contact.note: initial appointments (also shown as the 1-877-HOPE123 crisis line)

entries.name: Oasis Center - Youth Crisis Services and Emergency Shelter
entries.summary: Middle Tennessee's youth organization runs a 24/7 crisis line and a short-term emergency shelter (up to 10 young people at a time) for ages 13-17 who are in a very hard situation at home or school or need a safe place to stay. The page lists only the office address, not where the shelter beds are, so call the 24/7 line first.
entries.hours: Crisis line 24/7; main office Monday-Friday 9am-4pm

entries.name: Jean Crowe Advocacy Center (Metro Office of Family Safety)
entries.summary: A court-based center where advocates help victims of domestic and sexual violence with safety planning, danger assessment, crisis intervention, support groups, orders of protection, emergency food assistance and referrals. Walk-ins are welcome.
entries.hours: Monday-Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
entries.address: 100 James Robertson Parkway, Suite 114, Nashville, TN 37201

entries.name: Operation Stand Down Tennessee - Service Center (veterans only)
entries.summary: For veterans only; it is not open to the general public. Veterans can walk in to get connected to support, get help tracking down military records, receive mail, use a computer lab for job and benefits applications, and get hot meals on select days and hygiene kits when available. The group also runs a veterans suicide prevention program and a food-bag program called Operation Commissary. The page lists no opening hours, so call first.

entries.name: City Road Chapel UMC - Feast community meal and Showers of Blessing (Madison)
entries.summary: A Madison church that holds a free community meal for all comers on the 4th Sunday of each month, and runs Showers of Blessing, a weekly shower and laundry service for people who are homeless (a partnership with Community Care Fellowship and Laymen's Lessons). Showers close at 11 a.m. and laundry is limited to 15 loads a day. The church office can also arrange meal delivery to residents of Madison and Chippington Towers.
entries.hours: Community meal: 4th Sunday of each month at 5 p.m. Showers of Blessing: Mondays and Wednesdays 7 a.m.-12 p.m. (showers close at 11 a.m.)
entries.cost: The monthly meal is free to all comers

entries.name: Cumberland Heights - Hermitage outpatient program
entries.summary: A licensed outpatient addiction treatment center in Hermitage offering an intensive outpatient program (group and individual therapy several times a week, with family education), for people stepping down from residential care or who need an alternative to full-time treatment. It also treats co-occurring problems such as depression and anxiety. Call first; new patients arrive one hour before their first group to meet a counselor and finish paperwork. The location also hosts alumni care meetings and Alcoholics Anonymous (Seeking Sanity) meetings, which Cumberland Heights says it does not run.
entries.hours: Intensive outpatient, in person: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 9:00 AM-12:00 PM and 6:00-9:00 PM. Counseling, medication management and family services also available by telehealth.

lines.name: 211 Helpline (United Way of Greater Nashville)
lines.summary: Free, confidential line that connects people with local help for food, housing, utilities, health care, mental health and legal aid.
lines.hours: Live navigators Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-5 p.m. CST; online search 24/7
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
lines.summary: Call or text 988, or chat online, any time, free.

lines.summary: The state's 24-hour hotline run by the Tennessee Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Tennessee Sexual Assault Hotline (Sexual Assault Center)
lines.summary: 24-hour crisis and support line for sexual assault survivors.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: YWCA Nashville & Middle Tennessee Crisis & Support Helpline
lines.summary: Domestic violence help, including access to the Weaver Domestic Violence Center shelter, whose address is not public. Programs are free.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.summary: Metro Office of Homeless Services line for families facing homelessness; it cannot provide immediate shelter.

lines.summary: Metro Office of Homeless Services line for single adults facing homelessness.
