lines.name: Metro Nashville Police non-emergency line
lines.summary: For police help that is not an emergency. Call 911 for emergencies.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Second Harvest Food Bank of Middle Tennessee
lines.summary: Regional food bank; its Find Food page locates partner pantries and mobile pantries. The page does not say you can collect food at its warehouse, so use the locator.

contact.note: Martin Distribution Center, 331 Great Circle Road

lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Rachel's Vineyard national hotline (after abortion)
lines.summary: National hotline listed for people hurting after abortion. No Nashville-specific contact was found.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: AGAPE Nashville - Domestic Violence Helpline (Morning Star Sanctuary)
lines.summary: A 24/7 anonymous, confidential helpline for people facing domestic violence. Callers are assessed by phone and can be offered a safe stay at a secure shelter; the program also provides case management, counseling, a weekly support group, and free court advocacy for orders of protection. In immediate danger, call 911.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Mental Health Cooperative - Mobile Crisis and 24/7 Crisis Line
lines.summary: A 24/7 crisis line for Davidson County that can send a clinician to you at home, school, work or in the community, for adults, children and youth. Includes rapid assessment, safety planning and connection to follow-up care.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Mending Hearts - women's addiction treatment
lines.summary: A nonprofit long-term addiction treatment program for women (average stay three to six months) with medically monitored detox, medication-assisted treatment, residential treatment, recovery housing and outpatient care. It says it will not turn a woman away for lack of insurance or money. Apply online or call; the assessment team contacts you within 24 hours. The site lists only a PO box, so there is no walk-in address.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Renewal House - treatment for pregnant women and mothers
lines.summary: Substance use treatment for pregnant women and for mothers with custody of one or two children age ten or younger, with a long-term family program that includes housing, plus an intensive outpatient program for women. Call extension 114 to ask about eligibility. The site lists only a PO box, so there is no walk-in address.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Pregnancy Help Center - mobile clinic (Nashville area)
lines.summary: A mobile unit that travels to locations around Nashville offering free pregnancy tests, ultrasounds, and information about adoption, abortion and parenting. Book an appointment by phone. The site lists only a PO box, so there is no walk-in address.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Nurses for Newborns - Tennessee (free home visits for babies and new parents)
lines.summary: A free home-visiting program for families with babies in Middle Tennessee. Registered nurses check the baby's health and development, home visitors teach parenting skills, and licensed social workers help with mental health and home-environment concerns. Visits are arranged through a referral (a family, caregiver or agency can submit the form on the Tennessee page or call the office), not by walking in. Office hours 9 a.m.-4 p.m.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Nashville Diaper Connection (diapers through partner agencies)
lines.summary: A diaper bank that gives out diapers through partner nonprofits, healthcare providers and community organisations, not from a storefront. The Get Diapers page has a partner finder map and list; contact the partner directly for distribution dates and times. TennCare members may also be able to get a monthly diaper supply through their health plan, and a Diapers for Diplomas program helps parents in school or certification programs. The site lists only a PO box.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

cities.name: Memphis, Tennessee
cities.centre: Memphis city hall address (125 N Main St, Memphis, TN 38103) via US Census Bureau geocoder (onelineaddress, Public_AR_Current); used only to centre the map and measure distances

entries.name: Memphis Union Mission
entries.summary: The Mission's main shelter on Poplar Avenue, a men's emergency shelter. Call the shelter line to ask about a bed and who it can take.

entries.name: The Hospitality Hub
entries.summary: A walk-in point for people experiencing homelessness; it is the single entry point to housing and support services in Memphis.
entries.hours: Monday-Friday, 9 a.m.-12 noon and 1-3 p.m.

entries.name: The Salvation Army Memphis
entries.summary: Residential shelter services at its Jackson Avenue center, including a residence for single women and one for families. Call the matching hotline to ask about space.

entries.name: Calvary Rescue Mission
entries.summary: A faith-based shelter for homeless men in South Memphis, offering two meals a day, clothing, overnight lodging, nightly chapel and a discipleship program.

entries.name: Life Choices of Memphis (Raleigh)
entries.summary: Pregnancy medical clinic: pregnancy confirmation, limited ultrasound, STI testing and treatment, options counseling and practical help. It does not provide or refer for abortion. Same-day or next-day appointments may be available.

entries.name: Life Choices of Memphis (Poplar)
entries.summary: Midtown location of the same free pregnancy medical clinic: pregnancy confirmation, limited ultrasound, STI testing, options counseling and practical help. It does not provide or refer for abortion.

entries.name: Birthright of Memphis
entries.summary: Free, confidential pregnancy testing, mentoring, a Baby Steps program with baby supplies, and referrals. It does not perform or refer for abortion.
entries.hours: Monday-Thursday 9 a.m.-4 p.m.; Friday 9 a.m.-12 noon; closed federal holidays

entries.name: Shelby County Crime Victims and Rape Crisis Center
entries.summary: County center offering a 24-hour sexual assault hotline, crisis help and court accompaniment for victims of crime.

entries.name: Memphis Child Advocacy Center
entries.summary: Supports children who have been abused, especially sexually, and their families in Shelby County, and trains adults to protect children. It does not take abuse reports; use the state hotline for that.

entries.name: Kindred Place (formerly Exchange Club Family Center)
entries.summary: Counseling for children and adults, family coaching, parent training and supervised visitation, in English and Spanish. It takes some insurance and has self-pay options.
entries.hours: Monday-Thursday 9 a.m.-5 p.m.; Friday 9 a.m.-12 noon; 2nd and 4th Saturdays 9 a.m.-2 p.m.

entries.name: Hope House
entries.summary: Serves children and families affected by HIV and poverty, with early childhood education, therapy, HIV testing, housing and rent help, and a donation food pantry.
entries.hours: Office 9 a.m.-5 p.m.; Donation Pantry Monday-Friday 8:30 a.m.-12 noon (at 15 S. Idlewild St)

entries.name: Catholic Charities of West Tennessee (Jefferson Ave)
entries.summary: Food pantry run as a drive-thru in the parking lot; bring a photo ID and proof of address.
entries.hours: Monday-Thursday from 9 a.m. until supplies last

entries.name: Catholic Charities Midtown Outreach Center
entries.summary: Daily meal bags for people on foot or on the bus; no ID or proof of address required. Hygiene kits, food and basic clothing on Wednesday mornings.
entries.hours: Monday-Friday from 8 a.m. until supplies last

entries.name: Mid-South Food Bank
entries.summary: The regional food bank. Its Perkins Road site is its office; food reaches families through partner pantries and mobile pantries, so use the Find Food page or call before going.

entries.name: Memphis Dawah Association (Whitehaven Kulliye)
entries.summary: A Muslim community nonprofit that runs a food pantry for households in and around Whitehaven. Check before visiting, as schedules can change.
entries.hours: Every Saturday, 10 a.m.-12 noon

entries.name: Baptist Centers for Good Grief, Milla's House and Elle's Garden
entries.summary: Grief support in East Memphis, on the Second Baptist Church property. The centers state their services are free to anyone in the community.

entries.name: Heartland Adult and Teen Challenge, Memphis Training Center
entries.summary: Residential recovery program at its Memphis campus, open since 1972, working with students in the first two phases of the program.

entries.name: Harbor House Addiction Treatment Center
entries.summary: Residential treatment for adult men with substance use or co-occurring disorders; a nonprofit funded by the Tennessee Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse.

entries.name: YWCA Greater Memphis
entries.summary: Says it runs the only 24-hour emergency domestic violence shelter in Shelby County, with a 24-hour crisis and support helpline and advocacy for survivors of gender-based violence. The street address on its site is the YWCA's office; call the helpline first, because the page does not say where the shelter itself is.

contact.note: 24-hour Crisis & Support Helpline (also the main number on its site)

entries.hours: Crisis helpline answered 24 hours a day

entries.name: Agape Child & Family Services (Families in Transition)
entries.summary: Christian nonprofit whose Families in Transition program gives homeless Shelby County women who are pregnant or parenting (up to three other children), including those fleeing domestic violence, transitional housing for up to two years at no cost. Applicants must be 18 or older, single, free of felonies, and in school or work full time; its site says help is open to people who are not Christians. Agape also lists rapid rehousing for ages 18-24.

contact.note: Agape main line; the page says to call for rapid rehousing

entries.name: MIFA
entries.summary: Memphis nonprofit that runs a Hotline for Homeless Families for Shelby County residents with children under 18 and arranges family shelter placement for families who are literally homeless. Its site also lists rent and mortgage help to prevent eviction.

contact.note: Hotline for Homeless Families (Shelby County residents with minor children)

entries.hours: Office: Monday - Friday, 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.

entries.name: Room in the Inn-Memphis
entries.summary: A network of local faith communities hosts overnight shelter for small groups of individuals from November through March and May through September. It also runs a Family Inn for families with children (a 24/7 facility in the Medical District) and a recuperative care center for medically fragile people referred by healthcare providers. Call the office before going.
entries.hours: Office hours: M-F, 9am-5pm

entries.name: Memphis Union Mission - Intact Family Ministry
entries.summary: Christian mission program that lets families stay three to six months in a furnished three-bedroom house with no rent or utilities while they work and save, with Bible studies and counseling. It takes families with or without children but married couples only (no single-parent families), and families need their own transportation. Apply first: download the application and contact Reg Fowler.

entries.name: The Salvation Army Memphis Adult Rehabilitation Center
entries.summary: Residential 180-day work-therapy program for men struggling with substance abuse, with spiritual, social and emotional help and required classes and worship services. Applicants are 21 to 65, need a photo ID, and call the Intake Office for an interview; the page says you do not need insurance to enter.

entries.name: Memphis Recovery Centers, Inc.
entries.summary: State-grant-funded addiction treatment center offering adult residential treatment (long-term and short-term), a residential program for ages 13-17, partial hospitalization and family therapy. It accepts private insurance and TennCare, and says it has funds to treat Tennessee residents without insurance or the ability to pay; call admissions to ask whether you qualify.

entries.name: Memphis Area Intergroup Association of Alcoholics Anonymous
entries.summary: The local central office for Alcoholics Anonymous in Memphis, with a 24-hour helpline and a weekday office; its site lists A.A. meetings, local online meetings and information for new members.
entries.hours: Office: Monday - Friday, 8am - 4pm, closed daily 1pm - 2pm (follows Shelby County Schools on inclement-weather closures). Helpline: 24 hours.

entries.name: Celebrate Recovery at Sycamore View Church of Christ
entries.summary: Weekly Celebrate Recovery meeting at a church, in Room 1 at the back of the campus, for men and women, with or without a church background, including individuals and families battling addiction.
entries.hours: Tuesdays at 6:30 pm

entries.name: Capleville Community Food Pantry (Capleville United Methodist Church)
entries.summary: Church food pantry open Tuesdays for families in zip codes 38141 and 38125 who qualify for the program. The page does not list the qualifying rules or a sign-up process, so call or email the church first.
entries.hours: Tuesdays, 11:00 a.m. - 1:00 p.m.

entries.name: Colonial Park United Methodist Church mobile food pantry
entries.summary: Mid-South Food Bank delivers food to this church campus on the first and third Thursdays of each month, giving people in need an emergency 14-day supply; the page says everyone is welcome and lists no requirements. It does not give distribution times, so call the church office.
entries.hours: First and third Thursdays of each month (times not stated on the page)

entries.name: Faith Life Outreach - Hope for the Hungry
entries.summary: A Memphis church whose Hope for the Hungry ministry gives groceries to people in the community who have fallen on hard times, with a word of encouragement, access to its clothes closet and a hot meal. The page lists no requirements.
entries.hours: Every third Tuesday of the month, 5:30 - 7:00 PM

entries.name: St. Michael Catholic Church Food Pantry
entries.summary: Parish food pantry that gives out food on middle Saturdays of the month; ID is required to become a recipient. The phone number is the parish's general line, not a pantry line.
entries.hours: Middle Saturdays of the month, 9-11am

entries.name: HER Faith Ministries
entries.summary: Ministry serving homeless and needy women and children. Its site lists emergency food help (food vouchers), clothing and diapers for infants and toddlers, help with past-due rent or utilities, and prayer and spiritual guidance; call to ask what help is available now.
entries.hours: Contact page shows opening hours of 9:00 am to 4:30 pm (days not stated; call to confirm)

entries.name: Porter-Leath Connections (foster care and adoption)
entries.summary: Porter-Leath's Connections program provides foster care and adoption services for children from birth to age 18 who have been removed from their home, staffed by clinical staff 24 hours a day. Referrals come through the Tennessee Department of Children's Services, community service providers and schools, and self-referrals are accepted. The phone and address are Porter-Leath's main ones.

entries.name: First Congregational Church - Food Justice Ministry
entries.summary: Midtown church that serves a community lunch Monday through Thursday (it says 50-200 guests a day) and hands out pantry goods, produce, bread and other grocery staples on Wednesdays. The page states no requirements; call the church to ask about eligibility.
entries.hours: Community lunch Monday through Thursday, 11am-1pm; pantry Wednesdays, 11am-1pm

entries.name: St. John's United Methodist Church Food Pantry
entries.summary: Church food pantry in the Fellowship Hall (Peabody entrance); a valid ID is required, and it serves people living in zip codes 38103, 38104, 38105, 38106, 38107, 38108, 38109, 38111, 38112 and 38157. The page says food distribution depends on availability. The church's Swaddling Clothes ministry also gives diapers to Memphis families in need; its page lists no pickup days.
entries.hours: 1st & 3rd Thursdays of each month, 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM

entries.name: St. Luke's United Methodist Church - University Cluster Food Pantry and Sunday breakfast
entries.summary: Church in the University District that runs a food pantry on the second and fourth Thursdays of each month (its page says it serves all in need who come; the main requirement is to bring ID) and a free Sunday community breakfast open to the public. It also hands out Manna Bags, emergency snack bags with water and food, at the church.
entries.hours: Pantry: 2nd and 4th Thursdays, 9:30 am - 12:00 pm. Sunday breakfast: 8:00 - 9:00 am

entries.name: Grace-St. Luke's Episcopal Church - More Than A Meal
entries.summary: Sunday meal in Trezevant Hall for neighbors experiencing homelessness and hunger; guests arrive at 4:00 p.m. and the meal is served between 4:00 and 5:00 p.m.
entries.hours: Sundays, meal served 4:00 - 5:00 p.m.

entries.name: St. Mary's Soup Kitchen (St. Mary's Catholic Church)
entries.summary: Catholic parish soup kitchen that says it has operated continuously since 1870 and serves its community's poor, homeless and less fortunate six days a week. The page does not name the days or meal times, so call before going.
entries.hours: Six days a week (days and times not stated on the page)

entries.name: Calvary Episcopal Church - Sunday Neighborhood Breakfast and Clothes Closet
entries.summary: Downtown church that serves a Sunday morning neighborhood breakfast to about 180 neighbors experiencing homelessness and opens a clothes closet where homeless neighbors can choose clothes, blankets and toiletries.
entries.hours: Sunday breakfast 6 a.m. - 8 a.m.; clothes closet Sundays 6:15 - 7:45 a.m.

entries.name: Holy Trinity Community Church Food Pantry
entries.summary: Church food pantry open on the first and third Tuesday of each month; to receive food you must make an appointment by calling before noon on the Monday.

contact.note: Call before noon Monday for an appointment

entries.hours: First and third Tuesday of each month, 10-11 a.m. (appointment required)

entries.name: Friends For All Memphis - Food Pantry
entries.summary: Memphis HIV and sexual-health organization (HIV and STI testing, treatment, case management) that also runs a food pantry for its Memphis and Mid-South community. First-time visitors bring a photo ID and, if applicable, a Ryan White card; the page does not spell out who else qualifies.
entries.hours: Pantry pick-up Monday-Thursday, 9 am - 3 pm; first-time visits: front desk Monday-Thursday, 8:30 am - 3 pm

entries.name: St. Mary's Episcopal Cathedral - Hope and Food Ministry
entries.summary: Cathedral hunger ministry: individuals in need are invited to Morning Prayer in the Sisters Chapel on Saturday mornings, followed by a brown-bag breakfast. The phone number is the cathedral's general line, not a separate ministry line.
entries.hours: Saturdays, Morning Prayer at 9 am followed by breakfast

entries.name: Catholic Charities of West Tennessee - Downtown Outreach Center (St. Patrick Catholic Church)
entries.summary: Drive-thru mobile food pantry at St. Patrick Catholic Church where food boxes are placed into cars, run by Catholic Charities of West Tennessee. The phone is Catholic Charities' general number, the only one on the page, not a number for this site.
entries.hours: Tuesday-Thursday, 1:00-2:30PM

entries.name: Catholic Charities of West Tennessee - Mobile Food Pantry at St. Augustine Catholic Church
entries.summary: Drive-thru mobile food pantry at St. Augustine Catholic Church, run by Catholic Charities of West Tennessee, on the first Saturday of each month. The phone is Catholic Charities' general number, the only one on the page, not a number for this site.
entries.hours: First Saturday of each month at 9AM

lines.summary: Dial 211 to be connected to local help; every call is confidential. Texting is not mentioned on the page.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
lines.summary: Call or text 988, or chat online, if you are in emotional distress or thinking of suicide. Free and confidential, in Spanish too.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Memphis Crisis Center
lines.summary: A free, confidential 24-hour telephone line staffed by volunteers; it refers callers on to face-to-face help.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
lines.summary: Free, confidential support from advocates by phone, text or live chat. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Tennessee Child Abuse Hotline (DCS)
lines.summary: Call to report suspected child abuse or neglect in Tennessee, or use the secure online report. In an emergency call 911.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Memphis Police Department non-emergency line
lines.summary: For police matters that are not life-threatening. For emergencies call 911.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Rachel's Vineyard, Catholic Diocese of Memphis
lines.summary: Contact for post-abortion healing retreats hosted by the Catholic Diocese of Memphis. Ask Cathy for current retreat dates.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Tennessee REDLINE
lines.summary: Statewide referral line for substance misuse and problem gambling. Anyone can call or text for confidential referrals to addiction treatment; run by the Tennessee Department of Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Youth Villages Specialized Crisis Services (Memphis line)
lines.summary: Crisis line for children and youth up to age 18 in a psychiatric emergency in Tennessee, such as serious suicidal or homicidal thoughts, severe depression or out-of-control behavior. The page lists 866-791-9226 for the Memphis region and says specially trained counselors are available 24 hours a day in Tennessee.
lines.hours: Counselors available 24 hours a day (per the page)
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: The Women's Advocacy Center
lines.summary: Confidential, trauma-informed, Christ-centered support for women experiencing domestic abuse, sexual assault or stalking in Arlington, Bartlett, Collierville, Eads, Germantown, Lakeland, Millington, Northaven and unincorporated Shelby County. Call for a confidential consultation, or use the crisis line after hours. The page gives no street address.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Tennessee statewide domestic violence and sexual assault hotlines (TN Coalition)
lines.summary: The Tennessee Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence lists two statewide hotlines on its Find Help page: the Tennessee Domestic Violence Hotline and the Tennessee Sexual Assault Hotline. The page says support is available 24/7 and is completely free, confidential and safe, and it also lists local Shelby County programs.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Moriah House (Memphis Union Mission)
lines.summary: The Mission's long-term recovery program for women and their children: up to 15 women and their children live in individual suites with private baths, with a structured schedule of chores, exercise, meals, Bible studies and counseling. Clients come by referral; call, text or email to ask for help, or fill in the intake form on its site. The page gives no street address.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Memphis Morning Center
lines.summary: A Jesus-centered nonprofit giving prenatal and postpartum care, ultrasounds and labs, and classes to under-resourced pregnant women, at no charge. Book by calling. Appointments are by phone only; call and they will tell you where the clinic is.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

cities.name: Birmingham, Alabama
cities.centre: Birmingham city hall address (710 20th St N, Birmingham, AL 35203) via US Census Bureau geocoder (onelineaddress, Public_AR_Current); used only to centre the map and measure distances

entries.name: Firehouse Ministries
entries.summary: Emergency shelter for men 19 and older in downtown Birmingham. Men can walk in without an appointment or referral; a Continuum ID is needed and the staff can help get one. It also serves meals that anyone, including women, can eat.
entries.hours: First-time bed line-up by 5:30 p.m. (beds by lottery); day shelter 2-5 p.m. five days a week; lunch at noon

entries.name: Jimmie Hale Mission (Shepura Men's Center)
entries.summary: Christian-based mission offering a shelter and residential recovery program for homeless men, with other campuses for women and children. The mission says its program carries no cost.
entries.cost: Free (the site calls it a 100% no-cost program)

entries.name: First Light Shelter
entries.summary: Emergency shelter for homeless women and their children in downtown Birmingham, with access to housing programs.

entries.name: Pathways
entries.summary: Shelter and day program for women and children experiencing homelessness in Birmingham, with housing programs and an early learning center.
entries.address: 409 Richard Arrington Jr Blvd N, Birmingham, AL 35203

entries.name: The Salvation Army Center of Hope (Greater Birmingham)
entries.summary: Emergency shelter for men, women, children, families and veterans at one location; people seeking help are told to call or come to the Social Services Building.

entries.name: One Place Metro Alabama Family Justice Center
entries.summary: Domestic violence help for Birmingham and Jefferson County in one location: safety planning, help with protection orders and court accompaniment. Not a 24-hour service. The site has a quick-exit button.
entries.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:30-4:30, Friday 8:30-1:00; not a 24/7 service

entries.name: Prescott House Child Advocacy Center
entries.summary: Child advocacy center where children who may have been abused are interviewed in a child-friendly setting. The page says that in an emergency you should contact local law enforcement or the Jefferson County DHR hotline.

entries.name: Greater Birmingham Ministries
entries.summary: Offers help to people in crisis on weekdays, including a food pantry, clothes closet and financial help. Its food page says grocery distribution day is every third Friday; call to confirm how to get food.

entries.name: Positive Choices Pregnancy Resource Center
entries.summary: Free pregnancy testing, limited ultrasounds, consultations and resources for women, men, couples and families.
entries.hours: Monday-Wednesday 9 am-4 pm

entries.name: Alabama Pregnancy and Family Center (Crestwood)
entries.summary: Free and confidential pregnancy services and support. The center says it does not provide or refer for abortions.
entries.hours: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday 9am-4pm
entries.address: 1449 Medical Park South, Suite 300, Birmingham, AL 35213

entries.name: Alabama Pregnancy and Family Center (Vestavia)
entries.summary: Free and confidential pregnancy services and support, near Hoover and Vestavia Hills. The center says it does not provide or refer for abortions.
entries.hours: Mon, Wed, Thu 9am-4pm; Tue 9am-7pm; Fri 9am-2pm

entries.name: Alabama Pregnancy and Family Center (Fultondale)
entries.summary: Free and confidential pregnancy services and support in north Jefferson County. The center says it does not provide or refer for abortions.
entries.hours: Mon-Tue 9am-4pm; Fri 9am-2pm

entries.name: Her Choice Birmingham Women's Center
entries.summary: Free, confidential pregnancy tests, limited ultrasounds, counseling and parenting resources. The site also describes support for women and men affected by an abortion experience. Appointments preferred; walk-ins welcome.

entries.name: Community Grief Support
entries.summary: Free grief counseling and support groups in the Birmingham area for people grieving a death. It says it has no religious affiliation; groups often meet in churches.
entries.hours: Office hours Monday-Friday 9 am-5 pm
entries.cost: Free (the site says all services are free)

entries.name: The Amelia Center (Children's of Alabama)
entries.summary: Grief counseling for children and teens grieving a death and for parents grieving the death of a child. Appointments are in person.

entries.name: The Lovelady Center
entries.summary: Christ-centered residential program for women, including women with substance abuse issues or leaving incarceration; women can apply through the center.

entries.name: Recovery Resource Center (Crisis Center, Inc.)
entries.summary: Walk-in assessment, referral and peer support for people seeking help with substance use. Calling ahead is encouraged; arrive before 2:00 PM for an intake. Located on the 4th floor of the Cooper Green clinic.
entries.hours: Walk-ins accepted; arrive before 2:00 PM for an intake

entries.name: Pantry On The Bluff (Bluff Park United Methodist Church)
entries.summary: A volunteer-run church pantry that gives groceries, some household supplies and diapers to anyone in need, drive-through style, on the first Wednesday of each month. The church office also takes calls about emergency help with utility bills and food that the pantry does not cover (not rent); bring a photo ID and any bill.

contact.note: Church office; also the number for emergency assistance requests

entries.hours: First Wednesday of every month, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., first come first served

entries.name: Royal Divinity Ministries
entries.summary: A food ministry in the Wylam area of west Birmingham that has given out food and household items since 2015, with a drive-through pickup on Saturday mornings. It also offers case management (rent, utility and housing referrals and assistance), hygiene supplies, tutoring and training.
entries.hours: Open Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday; drive-through food pickup Saturdays 8:30 am to 11:30 am

entries.name: The Grace Place (Serving You Ministries), Bessemer food pantry
entries.summary: A food pantry in Bessemer run by Serving You Ministries, open four weekdays, Sunday afternoons, and one Saturday a month with Spanish-language service. The site does not state who qualifies, so call before you go.
entries.hours: Monday-Thursday 9 am-1 pm, Sunday 1:30-4 pm, 1st Saturday (Spanish) 9 am-1 pm

entries.name: Church of the Reconciler (United Methodist mission church)
entries.summary: A downtown mission church for people who are poor or homeless. Weekday mornings it gives out coffee and a sack lunch, lets guests use the office phone, and holds mail for people with no address (a photo ID is needed). It also has a case manager, and on Wednesdays staff from the ROSS recovery group are there to start addiction-recovery intake.
entries.hours: Office hours Monday-Thursday 9:00 am-2:00 pm; coffee and sack lunch Monday-Thursday mornings

entries.name: Urban Ministry (West End)
entries.summary: A faith-based nonprofit serving Birmingham's West End. Its WE Care program runs a food co-op that gives out groceries at no charge and offers a limited number of utility-bill help appointments each month; to ask for utility help, phone on the first Monday of the month between 9:00 and 9:30 am. Call the front desk to ask who qualifies.
entries.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.
entries.cost: Free (the food co-op is at no charge)

entries.name: Grace Episcopal Church Woodlawn, food pantry
entries.summary: A church pantry in Woodlawn that hands out groceries to households in need on Tuesday mornings. Go to the 58th Street door at the ramp.
entries.hours: Pantry on the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Tuesday of each month, 8:30-10:00 am

entries.name: YWCA Family Resource Center (Woodlawn)
entries.summary: A neighbourhood center in Woodlawn with adult-education and GED classes, tutoring, parenting support, financial-literacy classes, youth mentoring and, by appointment, case management. Registration is required for most programs.
entries.hours: Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-3 p.m.

entries.name: Children's Aid Society of Alabama (Birmingham office)
entries.summary: A child and family agency with its Birmingham office on the Southside. It runs a free six-week parenting class (EPIC) for Jefferson and Shelby County parents, and APAC support for foster, kinship and adoptive families.
entries.hours: 8:30am-5:00pm; open after hours by appointment

entries.name: East Lake Recovery Drop-in Center (East Lake United Methodist Church)
entries.summary: A recovery drop-in center in a church building on the east side, with free breakfast and lunch for participants and peer support for people working on addiction recovery.
entries.hours: Monday-Friday 9am-3:30pm

entries.name: Fellowship House, Inc.
entries.summary: A Southside nonprofit that provides treatment for alcoholism, drug addiction and co-occurring disorders. It holds open pretreatment classes twice a week; anyone interested can come straight to the site, and after class an intake team meets each person about next steps.
entries.hours: Open pretreatment classes every Tuesday and Thursday, 7:30-9:30 a.m.

entries.name: The Foundry Ministries, Men's Center (Bessemer)
entries.summary: A Christian residential recovery program for men overcoming addiction, in Bessemer. To start, submit the online application or phone; staff follow up the next business day. The Foundry's separate women's recovery program is at 1800 4th Avenue North, Bessemer (205-425-7737).

entries.name: Pregnancy Resource Center - Hueytown
entries.summary: A free, confidential pregnancy center in western Jefferson County, a division of Sav-A-Life Bessemer. All services are free.
entries.hours: Monday 9:00 am-4:00 pm, Tuesday 9:00 am-6:00 pm, Wednesday 9:00 am-4:00 pm, Thursday 9:00 am-4:00 pm

entries.name: Jessie's Place (Jimmie Hale Mission, women and children)
entries.summary: A Christian-based residential program for women and their children, with family rooms for up to 30 women and children. This is the mission's women-and-children campus, separate from the men's center already listed. Phone first to ask how to apply.
entries.cost: Free (the page says services at Jessie's Place are provided free of charge)

entries.name: Craig Crisis Care Center (JBS Mental Health Authority)
entries.summary: A crisis center run by the Jefferson, Blount, St. Clair Mental Health Authority for adults 19 and older who are in a mental-health or substance-use crisis. The Alabama Department of Mental Health lists it among crisis centers open around the clock to walk-ins. JBS's own page lists no hours, so phone ahead if you can; in immediate danger call 911 or 988.
entries.hours: 24 hours a day, every day, per the Alabama Department of Mental Health crisis-centers page (https://mh.alabama.gov/crisis-centers/); JBS's own page lists no hours

entries.name: Vestavia Hills United Methodist Church food pantry
entries.summary: A church food pantry with a drive-through distribution every other Wednesday morning, set up under the main campus parking lot, entered from Kentucky Avenue. Phone the church for the next distribution date. For immediate help with a specific need, the church has a separate benevolence line where you leave your name, phone number and need.

contact.note: Church office; call for the next distribution date

entries.hours: Drive-through every other Wednesday, 9:00-11:30 am; call for the next date

entries.name: Highlands United Methodist Church, Hospitality Hour (Five Points South)
entries.summary: A morning refuge for homeless neighbours with breakfast, mail and phone service, toiletries and a listening ear; laundry can be dropped off during the hour and is usually ready by the next one. On Wednesdays representatives from Cahaba Medical Care, One Roof and Recovery Services are there to meet guests, and a mobile medical unit gives free care and screening on the 4th Thursday of the month, 9:00 AM to 1 PM.
entries.hours: Hospitality Hour Monday-Saturday, 9:00-10:00 AM; laundry drop-off Tuesday-Saturday during the hour

entries.name: Avondale Samaritan Place (Avondale United Methodist Church)
entries.summary: The mission arm of Avondale United Methodist Church, based in the church gym. During the week anyone who stops by gets a snack bag and cold water; on Mondays there is a sit-down lunch where a social worker helps connect guests to resources. Three monthly food co-ops give out groceries from the Community Food Bank of Central Alabama. Its page gives no hours, so phone first.

entries.name: Grace Klein Community food drive-through at Liberty Church (Hoover)
entries.summary: A food drive-through site listed by Grace Klein Community, a Birmingham-area nonprofit. Its contact page lists this location under food support; it does not say who qualifies, so phone Grace Klein before you go.
entries.hours: Open every Monday-Thursday, 1pm-4pm
entries.address: 2732 Old Rocky Ridge Road, Hoover, AL 35216

entries.name: Grace Klein Community food drive-through at Bessemer Court (mobile)
entries.summary: A food drive-through site listed by Grace Klein Community, a Birmingham-area nonprofit. Its contact page lists this location under food support; it does not say who qualifies, so phone Grace Klein before you go. It is a mobile drive-through.
entries.hours: Open every second Friday, 1pm-3pm; in November and December 2026 it runs on November 6 and December 4

entries.name: Grace Klein Community food drive-through at the Jefferson County Family Court House
entries.summary: A food drive-through site listed by Grace Klein Community, a Birmingham-area nonprofit. Its contact page lists this location under food support; it does not say who qualifies, so phone Grace Klein before you go.
entries.hours: Open every fourth Friday, 1pm-3pm; in November and December 2026 it runs on November 20 and December 18

entries.name: Changed Lives Christian Center (affiliate of The Foundry Ministries)
entries.summary: A Christ-centered transitional housing center for men: a 56-bed center where men stay six months to two years with meals, clothing, basic medical care, recovery services and job-placement help, and it gives residents a mailing address and help getting a Social Security card or driver's license. Residents must be working or looking for work and pay fees toward living costs. Separately, each Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday hungry people are bussed in for a meal served by church groups, with monthly health screenings.
entries.hours: Meals for homeless neighbours each Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday (people are brought by bus)

entries.name: Brother Bryan Mission, New Life Fellowship
entries.summary: A nine-month Christian recovery program for men that deals with the causes of homelessness and addiction, ending with help from local business volunteers to prepare a resume and find a job. To apply, download the application from the site and email or mail it in; staff then interview the applicant by phone or in person, and applicants should check in by phone while it is reviewed. The page gives no walk-in hours.

entries.name: The Foundry Ministries, Women's Center (Bessemer)
entries.summary: A Christian recovery program in Bessemer where women work to overcome addiction and return to their roles in their families and communities through spiritual classes, guidance and employment-readiness training. Apply through the online form on the Foundry site (choose the women's program); staff follow up the next business day. The page gives no hours.

entries.name: Ann's New Life Center, Leeds location
entries.summary: A pregnancy medical center offering free, confidential support, information and pregnancy testing for people facing an unexpected pregnancy. Its page says no appointment is needed, you can stop by during open hours, and you will not be asked to pay. Leeds is on the east edge of the Birmingham area.
entries.hours: Open Monday and Wednesday, 10:00am-4:00pm

entries.name: Aletheia House Outpatient Center
entries.summary: The outpatient addiction-treatment site of Aletheia House, in the Finley Avenue area of Birmingham. Its locations page lists no hours and does not say whether walk-ins are accepted, so phone first.

entries.name: Aletheia House, Mother's Hope
entries.summary: Residential addiction treatment for pregnant women and women with children, run by Aletheia House. Its locations page lists no hours and does not say whether walk-ins are accepted, so phone first. The page prints the ZIP as 35204, which may not match this street, so the ZIP is left out here.

lines.name: 2-1-1 Connects Alabama
lines.summary: Free, confidential referral line for local help such as food, housing and utilities.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
lines.summary: National line for anyone in emotional distress or crisis: call or text 988.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Crisis Center, Inc. Crisis and Suicide Line
lines.summary: Local crisis and suicide line for the Birmingham area, answered by Crisis Center, Inc. Its page also lists a youth talk line and a senior talk line (205-328-8255).
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Crisis Center, Inc. Rape Response / SANE
lines.summary: Sexual assault support line run by Crisis Center, Inc.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: YWCA Central Alabama 24-Hour Domestic Violence Crisis Line
lines.summary: Answered 24/7 by a trained crisis specialist; the line offers safe shelter options for victims and survivors. Shelter locations are confidential, so reach shelter by phone.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Jefferson County DHR Child Abuse Hotline
lines.summary: To report suspected abuse or neglect of a child in Jefferson County. Alabama DHR asks callers to phone their county DHR or local law enforcement, not email.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Community Food Bank of Central Alabama - Find Food map and phone line
lines.summary: The regional food bank that supplies local pantries and runs mobile pantries. Its Find Food map lists free food by address, city and county. Food reaches the public through partner pantries and mobile pantries, so use the map or phone to find a distribution rather than going to the office.

contact.note: 2-1-1 Connects Alabama, listed on its page for emergency help

lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: R.O.S.S. 24/7 Helpline (Birmingham peer recovery)
lines.summary: A 24-hour helpline for people or family members struggling with addiction, from a Birmingham peer-recovery group. A chat line is also offered through its helpline website. Its page describes its peer services as free.

contact.note: Chat line named on its page

lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Image Clear Ultrasound Birmingham (free mobile pregnancy clinic)
lines.summary: A mobile clinic offering free pregnancy tests and ultrasounds. It parks at set stops through the week (its page lists Highway 280, Center Point, Irondale, Hoover, Bessemer and Homewood), but locations can change, so call or text to confirm where it is that day.

contact.note: Call or text to confirm the day's location

lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Family Promise of Birmingham
lines.summary: A nonprofit that helps families with children who are homeless or at risk of losing housing in North Central Alabama. There is no fee. To ask for help, phone the number below. Its page lists only a P.O. box, so it is a phone service, not a walk-in site.
lines.cost: Free (the page says there is no fee for services)
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Birmingham A.A. 24-hour answering service (Alcoholics Anonymous)
lines.summary: A 24-hour phone line for anyone who wants to talk to a recovering alcoholic. Its site carries the meeting calendar for Birmingham-area groups.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

cities.centre: Louisville Metro Hall address (527 W Jefferson St, Louisville, KY 40202) via US Census Bureau geocoder (onelineaddress, Public_AR_Current); used only to centre the map and measure distances

entries.name: Little Way Pregnancy Resource Center
entries.summary: Offers free pregnancy tests, ultrasounds and options consultations. The site says it does not provide ongoing prenatal care, perform or refer for abortions, or place for adoption.
entries.hours: Mon-Thu 9am-4pm; Fri 10am-2pm; Sat 9am-12:30pm

entries.name: BsideU for Life
entries.summary: Provides free, confidential pregnancy testing, ultrasounds, STI testing, options counselling, post-abortion support and life skills classes. It does not perform or refer for abortions.
entries.address: 701 W. Muhammad Ali Blvd., Louisville, KY 40203
entries.hours: Mon-Wed 9am-4pm; Thu 10am-7pm; Fri 8am-3pm; closed 12-1 for lunch; last client 45 minutes before closing

entries.name: Dare to Care Food Bank
entries.summary: The regional food bank. Call or come during food assistance hours for help finding food; its website has a tool to find a food pantry near you.
entries.hours: Food assistance hours: Mon-Thu 9am-4pm; Fri 9am-2pm; closed 12-1 daily

entries.name: St. Vincent de Paul Louisville Food Pantry
entries.summary: Volunteer-run pantry giving fresh produce, frozen meat and pantry staples. Its page says clients must live in ZIP code 40203 or on its campus and hold a pantry card; call to ask how to start.
entries.address: 415 E. St. Catherine Street, Louisville, KY 40203
entries.hours: Tuesday and Thursday 9am-12pm

entries.name: Sister Visitor Center (Catholic Charities of Louisville)
entries.summary: Choice food pantry, run with Dare to Care, where families shop for groceries once a month. Bring ID; the page mentions a service area, so ask by phone if you live outside it.
entries.hours: Mon-Fri 10am-2:30pm; closed the first Tuesday of each month and on Fridays in summer

entries.name: Fr. Jack Jones Food Pantry (Catholic Charities of Louisville)
entries.summary: Food pantry on the Holy Name Catholic Church campus in the south end, run by Catholic Charities of Louisville.
entries.hours: Pantry open Wednesday and Thursday 10:00am-12:00pm

entries.name: Jeffersontown Area Ministries
entries.summary: Community ministry supported by local faith communities that gives emergency food, rent and utility help, clothing and school backpacks to residents of ZIP codes 40299, 40023 and part of 40220.

entries.name: Wayside Christian Mission
entries.summary: Downtown shelter with a walk-in low-barrier shelter (no reservation needed) giving 24-hour emergency lodging and meals for men, women and families. Beds can also be reserved through Coordinated Shelter Access at 502-637-2337.
entries.hours: Walk-in low-barrier shelter open 24 hours a day
entries.cost: No charge for emergency shelter (per its FAQ page)

entries.name: Re:Center Ministries (formerly Louisville Rescue Mission)

entries.name: Southwest Community Ministries

entries.hours: Office Monday-Thursday 8:30 am-4 pm (separate pantry hours are not listed)

entries.name: Feed the City, Inc.

entries.name: Fairdale Christian Church - Celebrate Recovery

entries.summary: A food pantry in southeast Oklahoma City, run by Skyline, which also has a clothing Style Shop and an eye clinic (exams by appointment only). Come to the walk-in gate during the pantry hours listed.
entries.hours: Food Resource Center: Mon 1:00-5:00 pm; Tue 10:30 am-2:00 pm; Wed 1:00-4:00 pm; Thu 10:30 am-2:00 pm; Fri 9:00 am-noon; every 3rd Saturday 9:00-11:30 am. The walk-in gate opens Mon-Fri at 9:00 am.

entries.name: Reaching Our City Food Resource Center
entries.summary: A large food pantry in northwest Oklahoma City run by a faith-based community development group, plus a free community hot meal on Wednesday afternoons. Bring proof of your address and ID for each person getting food.
entries.hours: Pantry: Tue and Thu 3:00-6:00 pm. Free community hot meal: Wed 4:00-5:30 pm. Pantry closes if the Western Heights school district is closed for weather.

entries.name: Regional Food Bank Food & Resource Center (Moore)
entries.summary: A shopper-choice pantry run by the Regional Food Bank of Oklahoma in Moore, where you pick your own groceries once a month, with case managers who can point families to other help. ID and proof of residency are not required to receive food; it serves the ZIP codes listed on its page.
entries.hours: Mon 12:30-5:30 pm; Tue closed; Wed-Fri 10:00 am-3:00 pm; third Saturday of the month 9:30-11:30 am.

entries.name: Mid-Del Food Pantry
entries.summary: An independent food pantry serving hungry residents of eastern Oklahoma County (Midwest City, Del City and nearby ZIP codes), supported by local churches, businesses and civic groups. It serves only the ZIP codes listed on its Get Food page.
entries.hours: Mon, Wed and Fri 9:00-11:30 am and 12:00-2:00 pm. Closed on New Year's Day, MLK Day, Memorial Day, July 4, Labor Day, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and New Year's Eve.
entries.address: 322 N. Midwest Blvd., Midwest City, OK 73110

entries.name: Church of the Open Arms UCC Food Pantry
entries.summary: A church food pantry with no-contact box pick-up (drive-through or walk-up) on Fridays; no photo ID, proof of income or proof of residency is needed, and one person per household address may get groceries. The church also runs showers and a clothing closet on Friday afternoons.
entries.hours: Food boxes Fridays 4:00-6:00 pm; showers and clothing closet Fridays 3:00-6:00 pm.
entries.address: 3131 N Pennsylvania Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73112

entries.name: Manna Pantry at Together We Center (Yukon)
entries.summary: An emergency food pantry serving Canadian County families, run by volunteers and supported by local churches. It is first come, first served; arrive at least 30 minutes before closing. The same center has a Faith Clinic for uninsured medical care and a clothing boutique.
entries.hours: Mon 5:00-8:00 pm; Tue 3:00-6:00 pm; Wed 9:00 am-noon; Thu 5:00-8:00 pm; Sat 9:00 am-noon.
entries.address: 620 N. Cemetery Road, Building #2, Yukon, OK 73099

entries.name: The Salvation Army Oklahoma City Adult Rehabilitation Center
entries.summary: A residential rehabilitation program for adults facing substance abuse and other social, emotional and spiritual struggles. The Salvation Army says its residential programs are generally at no cost to participants. Call the Get Help Now number to ask about entry; no visiting hours are listed.

entries.name: NorthCare Crisis Site and Kelly Office (Edmond)
entries.summary: NorthCare's Oklahoma County crisis site is open 24 hours a day in Edmond for short-term assessment, stabilization and referral for mental health or substance-use emergencies. It serves adults 18 and older and children 5-17 who come with a parent or guardian. NorthCare lists the same Edmond address as its outpatient clinic.

contact.note: Edmond office (listed on the locations page)

entries.hours: Crisis site: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, every day of the year. Outpatient clinic at this address: Mon-Fri 8:00 am-7:00 pm.

entries.name: Oklahoma City Intergroup (Alcoholics Anonymous service office)
entries.summary: The local A.A. service office: stop in for help finding a meeting (it keeps coffee on and sells A.A. books), or call the hotline, which a recovering alcoholic answers around the clock. A Spanish-language line is also listed.
entries.hours: Office: Mon-Fri 9:00 am-6:00 pm; Saturday 10:00 am-3:00 pm. Hotline: 24 hours a day.

entries.name: City Care Night Shelter (Oklahoma City)
entries.summary: An overnight emergency shelter in Oklahoma City with men's and women's dorm rooms and family suites. It also offers meals, showers, clothing and hygiene items, ID recovery help, housing navigation and a pet hotel.
entries.hours: Nightly 6:00 pm-7:00 am (families with children 4:30 pm-8:00 am).
entries.address: 532 N. Villa Avenue, Oklahoma City, OK 73107

entries.name: Sisu Youth Services
entries.summary: A low-barrier drop-in center for young people ages 15-24 (hot meal, showers, laundry, clothing closet, food pantry, case management) and a 20-bed youth shelter that usually has a waitlist, so call first. Under-18s are prioritized for shelter beds, and the page says all are welcome.
entries.hours: Walk-in hours 4:00-7:00 pm daily; life-skill hours Mon-Fri 10:00 am-1:00 pm; drop-in by appointment 1:00-4:00 pm daily.

entries.name: Parent Promise
entries.summary: A parenting-support agency that runs voluntary parent education and home-visiting programs (including nurse home visits for first-time pregnant parents), a doula program and a Family Resource Center, with bilingual services. Call to ask which program you qualify for.
entries.hours: Office Mon-Fri 8:30 am-5:00 pm. Family Resource Center Mon-Fri 9:00 am-3:00 pm.
entries.address: 4323 NW 63rd St, Suite 200, Oklahoma City, OK 73116

entries.name: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of Oklahoma City (main office)
entries.summary: Walk-in guests can ask in the main lobby for bus passes, diaper assistance, snack packs, hygiene packs and a resource sheet. The agency also offers pregnancy support, family case management and emergency rent and utility help; its site says pregnancy services are free and confidential and you do not have to be Catholic.
entries.hours: Main lobby open to walk-in guests during regular business hours (hours not stated on the page).
entries.address: 1232 N. Classen Blvd., Oklahoma City, OK 73106

entries.name: Hope Pregnancy Center (Edmond)
entries.summary: A Christian pregnancy center offering free pregnancy testing, ultrasounds, options counseling and parenting classes, with baby supplies earned through the classes. Appointments are often same-day.
entries.hours: Mon-Fri 9:00 am-5:00 pm.

entries.name: Willow Pregnancy Support (Bethany)
entries.summary: An interdenominational nonprofit offering free pregnancy tests, limited ultrasounds, a prenatal clinic with SSM Health, counseling and education, baby supplies and peer support. Willow also runs a separate maternity shelter.
entries.hours: Mon-Thu 9:00 am-4:00 pm; Friday 9:00 am-2:00 pm.

entries.name: Project 66 Food & Resource Center (Edmond)
entries.summary: A client-choice food pantry in Edmond, run through the love of Christ, serving the ZIP codes on its Get Help page (Edmond, Arcadia, Guthrie, Jones, Luther, Meridian and two northwest Oklahoma City ZIPs). Bring a photo ID and proof of address. It cannot help with rent, utilities or other money.
entries.hours: Food pantry: Mon 10:00 am-noon and 6:00-7:30 pm; Wed 10:00 am-12:30 pm; Thu 10:00 am-noon; closed Tue and Fri (hours from the site's Get Help page).

entries.name: Breakfast on Boulevard (First Christian Church, Edmond)
entries.summary: A free hot breakfast and sack lunches served on weekday mornings since 1990, with no questions asked, funded and staffed by Edmond volunteers.
entries.hours: Weekdays 6:30-7:15 am.

entries.name: Samaritan House at St. John the Baptist Catholic Church (Edmond)
entries.summary: A parish ministry with a food pantry and help with rent and utilities for people in the parish area. A first-time visitor is asked to show photo ID and proof of residence; the page says that generally no one asking for food is turned away.
entries.hours: Mon-Fri 9:00 am-noon; closed Saturday and Sunday.

entries.name: Tuesday Outreach (Edmond First United Methodist Church)
entries.summary: A weekly hot meal and a welcoming place to rest, aimed at people experiencing homelessness. The page gives the time as 11:00 am-1:00 pm in one place and 12:00-1:00 pm in another, so call to confirm.
entries.hours: Tuesdays around midday (page says 11:00 am-1:00 pm and also 12:00-1:00 pm).

entries.name: NW 50th Street Church of Christ Food Pantry (Warr Acres)
entries.summary: A church food pantry open one morning a month with no appointment needed, for residents of ZIP codes 73008, 73122 and 73123. The page also lists a separate food closet by appointment, so call before going.
entries.hours: Food pantry: 2nd Tuesday of each month 9:00-11:00 am. Food closet: 2nd and 4th Tuesdays by appointment only.

entries.name: Peaceful Family Oklahoma
entries.summary: Free day-camp programs (ages 7-12 and 13-19) and family support groups for kids and teens affected by addiction in their families. Programs are by registration, so call (405) 601-2691 before visiting.

entries.name: NorthCare General Pershing campus (Oklahoma City)
entries.summary: NorthCare's main adult outpatient campus for mental health and substance-use treatment; emergency (crisis) walk-in services are available at its locations on weekdays. NorthCare says no one is denied services for inability to pay and offers a sliding fee scale.
entries.hours: Mon 8-5; Tue 8-7; Wed 8-5; Thu 8-5; Fri 8-3; Sat by appointment only; Sun closed.
entries.address: 2617 General Pershing Blvd., Oklahoma City, OK 73107

entries.name: Pivot (Family Junction youth shelter and drop-in support)
entries.summary: A youth agency whose Family Junction shelter gives a safe temporary place to live to young people 12-17, including youth in DHS custody, without parental support or who have run away. Youth 12-24 can also use drop-in support and a pantry with no appointment. Counseling has a sliding fee scale, and no one is turned away for inability to pay.
entries.hours: Office Mon-Thu 8:00 am-5:00 pm, Fri 8:00 am-noon. Drop-in support Mon-Fri 12:00-3:00 pm.

entries.name: Sanctuary Women's Development Center (Oklahoma City)
entries.summary: A Catholic Charities day shelter in Oklahoma City for homeless and low-income women and their children: a place to rest, showers and laundry, a computer lab, food for those who come in hungry, a community food and hygiene pantry, and social workers who help with housing and work. No hours are listed on the page, so call first.

lines.name: 211 Oklahoma
lines.summary: A free information line that connects Oklahomans with local help. Dial 211, or use live chat, text or the online search. The page does not print a phone number beyond the 211 code.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
lines.summary: Call, text or chat 988 for free, confidential help in a mental-health crisis.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Oklahoma Human Services Abuse and Neglect Hotline
lines.summary: Statewide line to report child abuse or neglect. For an emergency, call 911.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: YWCA Oklahoma City Domestic Violence Hotline
lines.summary: 24-hour hotline for domestic violence.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: YWCA Oklahoma City Sexual Assault Hotline
lines.summary: 24-hour hotline for sexual assault.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Oklahoma Safeline
lines.summary: State domestic violence line, listed as a 24-hour hotline on the YWCA page.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: NorthCare 24-hour Crisis and Mobile Crisis Line
lines.summary: Mental health professionals answer 24/7 for people of any age who feel out of control or have thoughts of suicide or of hurting themselves or others, in Oklahoma and Logan Counties. NorthCare's mobile crisis team goes to a home, work, school or anywhere in the community.
lines.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: La Luz Org (Latino survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault)
lines.summary: Confidential, free services for Latino victims of domestic violence, sexual assault and stalking, in a culturally and linguistically trauma-informed way; all are welcome. The page lists a 24/7 line and a separate office line.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Narcotics Anonymous helpline (Oklahoma City area)
lines.summary: The Oklahoma Region of Narcotics Anonymous lists this helpline for the Western Area, which covers Oklahoma City, for people looking for NA meetings and recovery from drug addiction. The same page lists a number to call from outside the Oklahoma City area and a text line for meetings by city or ZIP code.

contact.note: Western Area helpline, inside Oklahoma City
from outside the Oklahoma City area
text your city name or ZIP code for meetings near you

lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Oklahoma Adult & Teen Challenge (admissions line)
lines.summary: A faith-based residential recovery ministry for adults 18 and older (separate men's and women's programs) and boarding academies for teens. Its residential centers are in other Oklahoma towns (for example Stillwater for men), though the site lists 909 S Meridian Ave, Oklahoma City, as its main address. The site says affordable does not necessarily mean free, so ask admissions about costs.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Latino Community Development Agency (Spanish-language 24-hour crisis line)
lines.summary: A Latino community agency (prevention, treatment, health and wellness, youth programs and bilingual child development centers) that lists a Spanish-language 24-hour crisis line, Ayuda en Caso de Crisis. Its main office line is 405-236-0701 (office at 420 SW 10th Street, Oklahoma City).
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Hope Pregnancy Center mobile medical unit (Patty Ann, Oklahoma City metro)
lines.summary: A mobile medical unit run by Hope Pregnancy Center that visits Oklahoma City metro locations (including Midwest City and Moore) with free pregnancy tests and ultrasounds. Call for where it will be.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Positive Tomorrows (school for children experiencing homelessness)
lines.summary: A school and family support program for children and families experiencing homelessness, with transportation, meals and basic necessities. Call the number to ask about enrolling a child; the site lists only a PO box.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

cities.name: Savannah, Georgia
cities.centre: City hall address (2 E Bay St, Savannah, GA 31401) via US Census Bureau geocoder (onelineaddress, Public_AR_Current); used only to centre the map

entries.name: Savannah Care Center
entries.summary: Free, confidential pregnancy testing, ultrasounds, guidance, parenting education and baby supplies, and post-abortion support.

entries.name: America's Second Harvest of Coastal Georgia
entries.summary: The regional food bank (main branch).

entries.name: Union Mission
entries.summary: Housing programmes (Parker's House, Grace House, Magdalene House), a resource centre, permanent supportive housing and mental-health counselling.

entries.name: The Salvation Army — Savannah Corps
entries.summary: Local Salvation Army centre. Call to ask what help is available.
entries.hours: Mon–Fri 8:30am–4:30pm
entries.geocode: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Census geocoder found no match)

lines.name: United Way of the Coastal Empire 211
lines.summary: Referrals for food, health care, housing, utility bills, childcare and more for Savannah and Bryan, Chatham, Effingham, Liberty and Long counties. Not a 24-hour line and no walk-ins; allow 24–48 business hours for a reply.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (phone service); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: SAFE Shelter (domestic violence)
lines.summary: Confidential emergency shelter for victims of domestic violence and their children, a 24-hour hotline, and legal advocacy (outreach office 7373 Hodgson Memorial Dr., Bldg. 6, Suite 1, 912-651-0004).
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (shelter location is confidential); reach it by phone, text or online

lines.name: Mary's Place Sexual Assault Center of the Coastal Empire
lines.summary: Sexual-assault crisis line and support for survivors and their families.
lines.address: No walk-in address listed (address not published on the site); reach it by phone, text or online
